events.strFilename: Boxing 2026-09-19 John Hedges vs Pat Brown
events.strDescriptionEN: Two unbeaten British cruiserweights collide in Manchester as John Hedges faces Pat Brown in a significant domestic showdown at Co-op Live. Hedges enters with the greater professional experience and a 12-0 record, while Brown has made an explosive start to his paid career, winning each of his first six bouts inside the distance after representing Great Britain at the 2024 Olympics. The contest carries substantial stakes, with the vacant British and Commonwealth cruiserweight titles on the line alongside the WBA International and IBF Intercontinental belts. Hedges’ length and more measured boxing style provide an intriguing contrast to Brown’s aggressive, heavy-handed approach, making this one of the most notable all-British cruiserweight matchups of the year.
events.strResult: Pat Brown delivered the biggest win of his young professional career in Manchester, stopping John Hedges in the sixth round to claim the vacant British and Commonwealth cruiserweight titles. Fighting in front of his home crowd at Co-op Live, Brown gradually imposed his pressure and power against the previously unbeaten Hedges before a punishing body attack brought the contest to an end. Hedges had moments of success with his length and southpaw stance, but Brown’s aggression became increasingly difficult to contain as the fight progressed. The finish came in the sixth when Brown landed a decisive shot to the body that left Hedges unable to continue, extending Brown’s perfect professional record and giving the 2024 Olympian two major domestic titles in only his seventh professional fight.

events.strFilename: Boxing 2026-09-19 Isaac Cruz vs Nestor Bravo
events.strDescriptionEN: Isaac “Pitbull” Cruz returns to action in San Diego to defend his interim WBC super lightweight title against Puerto Rico’s Nestor Bravo in a high-stakes main event at Pechanga Arena. Cruz enters with a 28-3-2 record and 18 knockouts, looking to strengthen his position at 140 pounds after retaining the interim belt in a draw with Lamont Roach Jr., while Bravo arrives at 24-1 with 17 stoppage victories and the biggest opportunity of his professional career. Their aggressive styles and proven punching power give the matchup clear potential for sustained exchanges, while the supporting card adds another interim world-title bout as Jesus Ramos Jr. defends his WBC middleweight belt against unbeaten challenger Meiirim Nursultanov.
events.strResult: Isaac “Pitbull” Cruz retained his interim WBC super lightweight title with a sixth-round knockout of Nestor Bravo at Pechanga Arena in San Diego. The fight was physical and often untidy from the opening bell, with repeated clinches, warnings and a point deduction against Bravo in the fourth round after he threw Cruz to the canvas. Cruz remained composed through the disruption and gradually imposed his pressure, hurting Bravo with a left hook before producing the decisive finish in round six. A clean lead left hook badly stunned the Puerto Rican challenger and sent him to the canvas, prompting referee Thomas Taylor to stop the contest at 1:30. The victory moved Cruz to 29-3-2 with 19 knockouts and successfully extended his reign as interim champion.
